etym.s: [cf. Gk. νίζω for νιγ-ζω; Angl.Sax. nicor; Germ. Nix, Nixe.]

spans.s: mf(आ)n. (√ जन्) innate, native, of one's own party or country (with रिपु m. an enemy in one's own country, Hit.; m. pl. one's own people, Rājat.)
constant, continual, AV.; Br.; Mn.; MBh. &c. (in later Sanskṛt used as a reflex. possess. pron. = स्व, my own, his own, our own &c.)
नि-ज—कर्मन् n. one's own work
नि-ज—कर्˚म-बन्धन mfn. fettered by one's own works, MW.
नि-ज—घास m. ‘devouring his own’, N. of a demon, Hariv.
नि-ज—धृति f. N. of a river in Śāka-dvīpa, BhP.
नि-ज—पक्ष m. one's own party or adherents, Kathās.
नि-ज—मुक्त mfn. liberated for ever, Kap.
नि-ज—लाभ-पूर्ण mfn. engrossed in self-interest, self-satisfied, MW.
नि-ज—विनोद m. N. of wk.
नि-ज—शत्रु m. an enemy being in one's own self, an innate e˚, R.
नि-ज—स्व n. one's own property, MW.
N. of wk.
N. of an author, Cat.
N. of wk.
for one's own sake, for one's self, MW.
striking down, overpowering, RV.
shaking or trembling of the knees, TaittĀr.
g. यवादि
निजि—मत् mfn., ib.
= (or w.r. for) निर्-जिह्व, tongueless, Hir. i, 15, 5.
See नि-ग्रह् above.
(Desid. of नि√ ह्नु) wishing to conceal or deny, W.
नि-√ जूर्व् P. -जूर्वति, to consume by fire, RV.
नि-˚जु॑र् f. singeing, burning, destroying by fire, RV. ii, 29, 6.
